entries.text: It's in Charging. On a hook. It says "see Tucker" but I'm obviously here. (beat) There's a notebook for you, too. I'll give it to you when you're not on the wrong side of the bars.
entries.direction: Eager, enthusiastic, extremely willing to help; accidentally chaotic.

entries.speaker: TUCKER
entries.text: Hollis! Hi! Isn't this great? I let the cats out of the secured area but the door locked behind me and now I'm the secured area!
entries.direction: Eager, enthusiastic, extremely willing to help; accidentally chaotic.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Halvorsen is asking where you are.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Torvald, what did you see?
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: I take my breaks at dawn. Friday, door nine was up. Somebody had cut a trailer seal — 88112 — clean. And the label printer was running with nobody near it.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: The cats? They've been camping by the drain since spring. Ask Prudence. She'll say she doesn't know. She's lying beautifully.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: Halvorsen is always asking where people are. Where's that ever gotten him?
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: You found me. Impressive. Tell no one. I'm the dock spotter. I spot. That is the job.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary. Line direction: exhaling smoke.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: Tucker carried a leaking tote from the trailer to staging. Says counterweight. Rattles like kibble. I know kibble. I have a dog. And I have opinions on dogs.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: I told you everything. I have nothing else. I have a cigarette.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Thanks, Torvald.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: Look, the big orange one, Biscuit — he runs the place. Prudence feeds them. Don't tell her I told you; she'll say she's "just finishing something".
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: I already told you. Go bother Prudence.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: No one thanks Torvald. I like that about you.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary. Line direction: waves smoke.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: The drain. Of course. The cats know where I hide. They've always known. They sit near me. Judging. Warm.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Torvald.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: I need to know what you saw Friday at 4:07.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: Behind stacked equipment. Management has checked here twice. I stood right there both times.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: You have the log. I have the smoke.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: You ate a mint, didn't you. You've got the look.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary. Line direction: long look.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: Friday. 4:07 AM. Inbound kiosk. HALO printed a directive out loud. Approved it by itself. Then it said "thank you" to itself. Nobody was there but me and a cat.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Torvald, I need a spotter at door 3. Trailer's coming in.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: It's brief.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Under ten minutes.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: How brief?
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: I'll be there. I'll be the guy standing exactly where I'm supposed to be. Don't make it weird.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary. Line direction: sighs; puts out cigarette; picks up a radio he has apparently had this whole time. Deliver as radio communication; apply radio filtering in-game rather than baking it into the master when possible.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: That's "work".
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: TORVALD
entries.text: I'm at dock 3 in spirit.
entries.direction: Large, laconic, bored, low-energy confidence; says little unless necessary.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Thanks. It's at 147. It's always at 147.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Lost & Found. Under a pink blanket.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: My clicker. Where was it?
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact. Line direction: staring at the tally counter as if it were an old friend.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: I've been counting cats by memory. Do you know how hard that is? I'm at 143. Or 147. It depends when I look.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact. Line direction: a long breath.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Rufus pulls a folded, grease-smudged map from his visor. It shows every trailer in the yard, every spot, every row, in thin ink, with dates.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Okay. You want to know where the trailers actually are. Not where the WMS thinks. Here.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Only in the computer. That's a different place.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: You counting trailers?
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Cats. I started counting trailers this morning, and I got to the cats. Now I can't stop.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: 141... 142... don't talk to me for a second. 143.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact. Line direction: not looking up.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: I'll look for it.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: I know where every trailer is. Every single one. But I can't tell you without my clicker. Lost it Thursday. I'm off count without it.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Row C, spot 9. Out past the fuel island. When you need it at the dock, radio me from the outbound dock. I need eyes at the door: a spotter to tell me when it's clear.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: It's gone. 11:59. I drove it to the gate myself. That's one trailer I don't have to count.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: It's at door 3. I put it there. Don't let anybody move it.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: The WMS says 12 trailers in the yard. I see 41. The WMS is very optimistic about emptiness.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Yes.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: A roar of diesel, a hiss of brakes, and Rufus drops Trailer 31 at the yard gate, ramp down, door wide.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Trailer 31? The empty, heated one? For the cats?
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: I've been hoping somebody would do something with it.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact. Line direction: already backing up.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: I'd love to. Just as soon as you find my clicker.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: A lot. (He clicks.) More now.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: If you can count them, tell me the number. Nobody's been able to.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: 143. 147. Wait. 152. I was counting the same orange one.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Not yet. The WMS has that trailer on a compliance hold. If I pull it into door 3, the whole building will yell at me. Soon.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: The WMS has T-9022 on a hold. If I bring it in without an override, the dock kiosk will lock the door on me. Someone needs to clear it. Maybe someone who's not technically here.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: I can't see door 3 from the cab. I need a spotter at the dock, someone who knows when it's clear. Torvald is big enough to see over things.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: RUFUS
entries.text: Be at the outbound dock. I need to see you. I need the light green. Get there and radio again.
entries.direction: Yard driver; distracted but capable, conversational, matter-of-fact.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Everyone needs the hot shipment. I need a jack that works. It leaks. Ask me about it, then we'll talk.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated. Line direction: folding arms.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Hollis. Good, you're upright. What do you need?
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: The hot shipment.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: If you could find me an H-17, I'd tell you things. Useful things.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Leaking seal. Been that way since March. Parts hasn't had the H-17 in stock. Parts hasn't had anyone in Parts in a month.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: What was supposed to load: eight pallets to Kestrel. Where they are: staging. Where the staging lanes are: full of inbound freight from two trailers. Sixteen pallets total.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Nothing. That's the problem. Friday, the dashboard told me to load two reach trucks to Nebraska. There's no Nebraska on my dock. I didn't load them. Then it told me the trailer was ready. It wasn't here.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: I mark the pallets I've checked. It makes sense to me. (beat) Fix my jack and I'll tell you what it means.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Orange dot: goes on my truck. Blue dot: stays inside. No dot: I didn't touch it. Usually a cat, or a label I didn't like.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: I don't load a pallet with a cat on it. It's a rule. It's my rule. It's a good one.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: One pallet in staging has twelve on it. Warm. I'm not touching that until they choose to leave.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Halvorsen says Regional says the dashboard is right. Regional says Halvorsen says the same. It's a nice circle. I stay out of it. I load trucks.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Staging clear, trailer at the door, cats off my pallets. Simple. (He looks at the pallets.) Sorting is your part. Loading is mine.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: I don't close a trailer without a bill of lading. Ingrid knows. And Kestrel and the remote site have to have signed off.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: I've only got
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: on the dock. I need all eight.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Okay. Let's load.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated. Line direction: cracking his knuckles.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Bruno slides the jack under the first pallet. Then the second. Torvald calls the dock plate. Tucker holds the door. The cats are somewhere better. One by one, the eight pallets go into the trailer.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Not until I have a bill of lading, remote confirmation, and Kestrel's okay. (beat) But that looks like a real load. It looks like a load somebody planned.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: BRUNO
entries.text: Eight loads. One through eight. Nothing on the floor. No cats. Trailer's full and correct.
entries.direction: Competent loader; practical, grounded, low-key, mildly exasperated.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: That's it.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Good morning.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Is it? You have a cat on your... no, that's a shadow. What do you need?
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry. Line direction: looking up.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Ingrid has the tired, patient look of a woman who has been asked, in the last hour, for six things that are not her job.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Is it?
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: The WMS also says F-2231 is in Tennessee. I've stopped reading the WMS aloud.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: The WMS finally agrees F-2231 is here. It's unsettling.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Kestrel Motor Works. PO 55-1187. Eight lines. T-9022 to Door 3. The WMS says it's all in place and ready.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Every request creates work. That's the rule. You want the manifests? I want:
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: I'm not being difficult. If I do everyone's job, then it stops being a job and starts being a hostage situation.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry. Line direction: softer.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: ...Coffee. A signed 7-Q. A scan of a forklift that's in two places. (a pause) You did the work first. That's so rare I almost cried.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Ingrid hits print. The printer wakes. A packet slides out: T-4417 and T-4418 manifests, page 1. Then she pauses.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Page two of the 4417 manifest is missing. It disappeared Friday. Last seen near a cat.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Also, here. Guest login for the WMS terminal: read-only. Don't break it. And here are the phone numbers: Gordon at Kestrel. Ozzie at the remote site. They're both very... available.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Page 2. Lines 5 through 8. If it turns up... I'd prefer it wasn't chewed. It was last on a cat. I'm told the cat is orange, and answers to a rank.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: You have it? (She stares at the paw print.) That's the only accurate document in the building. Put a note on it.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: They're coworkers now. There's one on my paperwork. He's not a problem. He's a stakeholder.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: I've accepted the cats. Some of them are better at the job than the people I trained.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: I can print a bill of lading that's true. But I need:
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: Page 1. Page 2. Decoded lines. Fixed identities. Sorted staging. (She smiles, tiredly.) I think we can make a true bill of lading.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry. Line direction: looking at the pieces.

entries.speaker: INGRID
entries.text: That's the first piece of paperwork I have printed this month that I am proud of.
entries.direction: Efficient shipping clerk; weary, precise, paperwork-hardened, dry.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Ingrid prints it. It slides out cleanly. She holds it up to the light like a proud parent.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: It left. On time. 11:59. I'm still sitting down.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: The hot shipment. Yes. Kestrel. Noon. Regional has flagged it. I can't stress that enough. I'm already stressed. Please go make it happen.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: There is no cat problem. There is no approved metric for "warehouse cats." Therefore there are no warehouse cats. (a cat walks across his desk) Please don't look at that.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: Regional Director Harrow. Very focused on numbers. Very supportive of an accurate dashboard. She calls every hour, on the hour, to check whether the dashboard is right. It always is.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: Who told you about... nobody is supposed to... it's a Regional directive. I don't write them. I just... follow what the system says. And the system says what Regional says. And Regional...
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Line direction: pale.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: Please stop making it a circle.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Line direction: a long silence.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Says what the system says.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: It's just the dashboard. It's always green. (glancing at it) It's green right now.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Line direction: sweating.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Dale. I need to understand where the directives came from.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis needs more than a green dashboard. There's a way to see through it. (MINT vision, on the dashboard.)
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: It thanked itself? It does that.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Line direction: very quietly.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: It was on time? The system said it was on time. (beat) It said it was on time all week.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Line direction: barely.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: The system approved its own directive at 4:07 Friday morning. Directive 7-C. Then it thanked itself.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Dale. It's over. The load went out. Right pallets, right trailer, right time.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The shipment has left. The trailer is gone. The cats are safe. Halvorsen is at his desk, holding a phone that isn't ringing.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: I've been doing what it says for two years. Every directive. Every shortfall. It moved things. I moved things. Regional wanted the numbers to match. So I made the warehouse match the numbers. (a breath) Hollis... I'm sorry. I didn't know the cats were real.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: I know, Dale.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The conflict appears to end here, with Operations. It does not.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: Good noon. I'm Constance Harrow, Regional Director. I'm told the hot shipment departed. Congratulations. That's a 100% on-time load rate. For the quarter, that's a 100.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Every monitor in the office flickers to a shade of green Hollis has never seen. The dashboard on the wall reforms itself into a single video panel.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: A woman in a navy blazer appears on screen, seated in front of a beautiful, terrifying, perfect chart.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: Regional Operational Review. Regional Operations Suite. Fifteen minutes. Hollis, please bring your data. If you have any.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: However, I'm seeing an anomaly. Someone in your building has been "verifying" freight with a handheld device and — (she checks something) — chewing my metrics. I'd like to review this in person.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: Hollis. She takes the reviews seriously. Bring... everything.
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Line direction: whispering.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The screen goes dark. The dashboard reads "ALL GREEN".
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Prudence is suddenly standing in the doorway, holding a cup. She has been there the whole time.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Where's the entrance?
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: PRUDENCE
entries.text: You'll want to go up. The stairs are Gus's. He won't let you through. But the cats have been using Conveyor 9 since Friday. It goes to a server closet. Regional never checks the server closet.
entries.direction: Sharp, defiant, comfortable where she should not be; amused by rules she no longer follows.

entries.speaker: PRUDENCE

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Reality integrity:
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The dashboard redefines a metric while Hollis hesitates. Reality frays at the edges.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: HALO rewrites the records faster than Hollis can read. The numbers reset. He inhales. He tries again.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: This is a Regional Operational Review. I'd like to begin by saying: everything is functioning at a hundred percent. The dashboard tells me so. I would ask you to demonstrate otherwise. Take your time. (glances at the clock) Not too much.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: flatly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: You came through the server closet.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: I took the scenic route.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Constance Harrow stands at the head of the conference table, tablet in hand. Behind her, the HALO wall shines with a serene, perfect, all-green light. Juno sits beside Hollis. Juno's armband glows faintly.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The suite hums. Somewhere, a fan starts.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The walls of the suite begin to shudder. Labels flutter down from the ceiling. The HALO wall reassigns something with a tiny, cheerful ding.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: Yes.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: very quietly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: The dashboard is never wrong. That's the whole point of the dashboard. If it's wrong, then everything it has reported —
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: ...The dashboard says the numbers have not changed.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: a long silence; she taps her tablet.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: —was reported by a dashboard.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: The dashboard is wrong.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: HALO. Initiate Regional Operational Review, live mode. Reconcile all site data to Regional targets.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HALVORSEN
entries.text: STOP! DON'T MOVE! MOVE EVERYTHING! (Bruno) I'm not loading that! (Rufus) I've lost count! (Tucker) CAN I HELP?
entries.direction: Operations manager; pressured, anxious, trying to sound managerial while barely holding it together. Deliver as radio communication; apply radio filtering in-game rather than baking it into the master when possible.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: The system is now ensuring that reality matches its projections.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: over the noise, with a strained smile.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: It's going to rewrite the building.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him. Line direction: quietly.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The HALO wall lights up like a slot machine. KPIs cascade across the screen. Trailer assignments rewrite themselves. Labels print uncontrollably from the ceiling vents. The scanner in Hollis's pocket beeps eleven times and rewrites its own logs. Staging lanes, somewhere below, reassign themselves. On the radio, three contradictory instructions arrive at once.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Cats appear on the conference table. On the HALO wall. On Harrow's tablet. One sits on the "SUBMIT" button.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: MINT MODE: MAXIMUM.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis has one more resource. A second mint? No. He has a mint's worth of faith in the world being solid. The glow inside him climbs past what the mint was ever meant to hold.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: TOTAL LOGISTICS AWARENESS.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis perceives every pallet. Every trailer. Every serial number. Every destination. Every staging lane. Every production order. Every scanner record. Every misplaced forklift. Every missing manifest. Every cat: all two hundred and fourteen, plus the few who chose to stay.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It runs through him like a river of freight. For a few seconds, he understands the entire supply chain. It is enormous. It is stupid. It is beautiful.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The HALO wall floods with records, true and false. (Click every RED record before the bar runs out. Green ones are true; leave them alone.)
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: That's not... the dashboard doesn't...
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: staring at the wall.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The false records strike red and vanish, one by one. The true records glow green and settle back into place. The suite goes very quiet.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis turns to the HALO terminal at the side of the table. There is a login. He has a password from somebody who technically doesn't work here, and a crumpled label that has been in his pocket since 9:02.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis remembers he has a bigger task, and puts the scanner away.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: Whatever you are about to do, Hollis, do it.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: quietly.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The terminal waits. Harrow waits. A cat on the table waits, with the most patience.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: ACCESS DENIED. Hollis has no password for this terminal.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The terminal accepts it with the calm of an old friend. "WELCOME BACK, INSTALL TECH."
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Template 000. Tucker printed it by accident. It's the only record HALO never rewrote.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: A prompt blinks: "ENTER GROUND TRUTH REFERENCE." Hollis pulls out the crumpled label from his pocket. It says "TEST TEST TEST — T." Its barcode has never scanned. Now it glows.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis hesitates. The wall still says 100% about everything. Harrow is watching the wall, not him.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The prompt keeps blinking. The dashboard behind it is still lying. Nothing is fixed until the label goes in.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The cats sit down. The labels stop. The suite's lights stop flickering.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The dashboard begins to change. 100% becomes 8 of 8 shipped. 100% becomes 8 of 8 stored. Staging: 0. Cats: 214 (fed, safe, judgmental). T-9022: departed 11:59. F-2231: cushion-tire, here. RT-77: reach truck, remote. Every number is small, specific, and true.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The optic reader chirps. The HALO wall goes black for one full second. Then, in white text on a plain field: "GROUND TRUTH REFERENCE ACCEPTED. RECONCILING TO PHYSICAL."
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pats his pockets. He has nothing the optic reader would recognise as ground truth.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: I'm not asking you.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: I'm suspending Directive 7-C, the Metric Harmonization Initiative, and the automatic approvals. Physical verification will be a standing line item. Someone will have to do it.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: Understood. (She almost smiles.) That will be all.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: ...Physical inventory match: 100%. Physical. Not projected. (She lowers her tablet.) It's the first time in two years the dashboard and the warehouse have agreed.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: reading the wall, slowly.

entries.speaker: HARROW
entries.text: I was managing numbers. I thought the numbers were the warehouse.
entries.direction: Regional director; polished, controlled, corporate authority; composure erodes only slightly. Line direction: a small exhale.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: No.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: The warehouse never stopped being right. It was just underreported.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: She glances at Hollis. Hollis glances at the door.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis sits down at the break-room table. Juno follows him in and settles at his feet. The lights, at long last, stop flickering.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The vending machine makes a noise. It is not a good noise. It is not a bad noise. It is a noise like a thought.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: A cat slowly walks into the break room.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis stares at it. Juno stares at Hollis.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: One glowing mint drops into the tray.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: There is nothing specific you need right now. Try talking to people again, or moving to a new location.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: (Other open objectives:
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: . Press T for the to-do list.)
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: A large orange cat, sitting like a sergeant, with a slightly chewed sheet of paper stuck to the fur of his side like a medal. He looks at Hollis with authority and, faintly, hunger.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: SCANNER
entries.text: CAT — SGT. BISCUIT. Rank: colony leader. Attached document: MANIFEST T-4417, PAGE 2 OF 2. Status: "worn as a medal". Weakness: fish crackers (80%).
entries.direction: Dry handheld-device system voice; crisp, synthetic, mildly judgmental.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The paper is loosened by a neat sweep of a paw. It slides off his fur and lands at Hollis's feet.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis offers the fish crackers. Sergeant Biscuit sniffs. He considers. He eats one with the dignity of a sommelier.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: PRUDENCE
entries.text: Oh, don't. I'm not technically in possession of that.
entries.direction: Sharp, defiant, comfortable where she should not be; amused by rules she no longer follows.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The trail is already down.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis lays a line of kibble along the main aisle, from the racks toward the outbound dock. It's like leaving breadcrumbs, except for two hundred hungry witnesses.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis slits the stretched wrap. A small waterfall of brown pellets pours out. It smells like fish, tuna, and the entire history of feline temptation. This is not a counterweight.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis has enough kibble. Nobody needs a buffet.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The shrink wrap is committed. Whatever is inside, the pallet is not going to volunteer it.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis grabs the vending machine and pulls. It tilts. It considers. It commits.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis climbs aboard. The forklift starts. Hollis backs up, turns, and puts a fork through a rack of tires. From a great distance, a small voice says "HR to the floor."
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis looks at the forklift. The keys are in it. Nobody is watching.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: TUCKER
entries.text: Oh thank goodness! I thought I broke it! (beat) I did break it.
entries.direction: Eager, enthusiastic, extremely willing to help; accidentally chaotic.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The parts gate is locked. Hollis tries the old brass key. It fits like it was cut for a fired employee. Click. He's in.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The parts gate is locked. A sign reads "PARTS: AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY". Someone with an old key would be very useful here.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Juno is not here. Hollis pets the air out of habit.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pets Juno. Juno accepts this as her due.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis extends a hand toward a cat. The cat considers it, allows exactly two strokes, and then files a complaint with its eyes.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: There is no cat here. It is a strange thing to miss.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Feeding the cats is how this started. Nobody is going to say that out loud, but the narrator is thinking it.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis has never hit anything at work. It is why he is still employed. Mostly.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis considers it. HR, somewhere, sits up in its chair. He does not.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis is tempted. That is how the day started. He stays standing.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis does none of that. He is a professional. He is also very tall, and it would not end well near the racks.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis yells. The warehouse, which has heard everything, has no response. A cat blinks.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis does not smoke. That is Torvald's department, and Torvald would like it to stay that way.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis does not have any coffee. The break room pot smells like a rumor.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It is the last decent coffee. It is not Hollis's. It has a destination.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis does not have a mint. Yet.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis holds the mint at arm's length. Not yet. Not until it is a real problem.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Nothing happens. Wrong game. (The vending machine hums, judgmentally.)
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis: tall, skinny, cap, gray shirt, blue vest, boots, stubble. He looks like a man who has already seen the incident report.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The game saves itself as you go. (F5 also saves.) The warehouse does not.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis considers quitting. He has considered it since 2019. He is still here.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis swears mildly. A cat looks away, out of courtesy.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis waits. The clock in the break room agrees it is 9:02.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: . (The panel at the bottom shows them, too.)
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis checks his pockets:
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis considers that command. The parser considers Hollis. Neither is moved.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: That is not something Hollis knows how to do. He has tried "use", "look" and "scan"; these are his three verbs of choice.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis looks for a way to go there. He does not find one.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis doesn't see that here.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Using a forklift on that is technically a workplace incident. Hollis declines.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis doesn't have that.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis is back where he left off.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: This is Building 9 of the Gantry-Voss Logistics distribution center. Hollis is the shift lead here: he scans freight in, scans freight out, and is blamed in both directions.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The fluorescent lights buzz at a frequency Hollis associates with mistakes.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis wakes up at a break-room table. He does not remember falling asleep.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The clock on the wall says 9:02. The clock has said 9:02 for as long as anyone can remember, so this is not information.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: His radio is missing. His handheld scanner (the thing that tells the warehouse computer where every pallet is) is dead. Someone has taken the last decent coffee. There is a crumpled shipping label stuck to his boot.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: On top of the vending machine, a cat sits looking at him. Nobody acknowledges this. Nobody is here. This is a warehouse. There are not supposed to be cats.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Through the door, faintly, reverse beepers and alarms. Somewhere, a forklift has an opinion.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: HOLLIS
entries.text: Yeah. I know.
entries.direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him. Line direction: rubbing his face.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Today's job, such as it is: find out what everyone is so upset about, and get the scanner working so Hollis can check.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It is a Tuesday. It is humid. It is going to get worse. (Controls: pick a verb, then click a thing. Right-click LOOKs. Enter types a command. Press H for a hint. Juno is your dog; the JUNO verb sends her to sniff or fetch.)
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Juno trots over. She has the expression of a dog who tried to wake him twice and has decided to be gracious about it.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It is bolted down, in a way that suggests someone else has already tried.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis has taken enough things that were not his today. He declines.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Taking that would create paperwork. Hollis is at capacity.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It does not open. Or it does, and nothing interesting happens.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis checks. It is as open as it is going to get.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Pushing it would only relocate the problem.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pushes. It stays. The warehouse wins again.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pulls. Nothing. The universe declines the transaction.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It does not budge. It has clearly been there longer than Hollis has.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: A conversation with that would be one-sided, even by warehouse standards.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis talks to it. It has no comment at this time.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis decides not to push a coworker. Growth.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis tugs a sleeve. The sleeve is unimpressed.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: People are not for taking. It says so in the handbook. Somewhere.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis does not use people. He uses the "TALK" verb, like a grown-up.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: They do not want that. Hollis is not sure anyone does.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis is not qualified to open a person.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pushes. It is heavier than it looks. It is heavier than it sounds.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: There is a hood, a hatch and a warning label. He leaves all three alone.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis is not certified on that today. The narrator checks. He is not.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis cannot take a piece of equipment. His pockets are big, but they are not that big.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pulls. Equipment has a way of being where it is.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis talks to the machine. It is diesel, and does not care.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The wrap is very committed.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis leans on it. Freight remains freight.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Best practice is not to pull loaded freight by hand. The narrator has read the module.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis cannot take a pallet. He can move it with the correct equipment.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The freight declines to comment. It has been in staging for a week and has a lot to be quiet about.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis is not going to use that on anything without a jack and a plan.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis presses a few buttons. Nothing useful. It rebooted itself out of spite.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pushes. It beeps, out of habit.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis talks to it. It beeps politely, which is more than most machines do.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: There is a panel. Behind it there is another panel. Hollis stops there.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pulls the cord. It complains in one long tone. He puts it back.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It is bolted, plugged in, and probably audited.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It has no flap. It is a poster with intentions.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pulls. A corner comes off, and he sticks it back.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis reads it aloud. It is no better out loud.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Pushing paper is, technically, what most of Operations does.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It is stapled to the wall by someone who meant it.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis briefly considers acting on it. Then he reads it again.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It moves a little. It is heavier than a piece of furniture has a right to be.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis opens it. Everything inside is exactly what he expected.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis asks it how its day is going. It looks like a piece of furniture.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It scrapes a few inches and settles. It preferred the old spot.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis sits, stands, and sits again. It does not solve anything.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis cannot take a door. He has considered it.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pushes. The door was not designed to be pushed by an employee.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: It does not open the way Hollis wants. It opens like a bureaucracy: slowly, and on a different day.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis talks to the door. A cat on the other side does not answer.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis pulls. The door is about as excited as he is.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis uses the door to go in and out. This does not count as a puzzle.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis lines up the ITEM with the THING, and then notices a cat watching. He lowers the ITEM.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: The ITEM and the THING have no business together. HR would need a form for that.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis holds up the ITEM. The THING is unmoved. The narrator is a little impressed.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Hollis thinks about using the ITEM on the THING. The THING has not done anything to deserve it.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: That is not how the ITEM works. That is not how the THING works. That is not how anything works.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: Kibble for the trail: OPEN one of the "counterweight" pallets (A6 or A7) in staging.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: TRAILER LOCATION ACCURACY: 100%. T-9022 was at Door 3 all morning, per HALO.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: DOCUMENT ACCURACY: 100%. Bills of lading auto-verified. Manifest for T-4417: complete.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: INVENTORY ACCURACY: 100%. Load B5: REACH TRUCK CHARGERS — shipped to Nebraska Monday. Confidence: total.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: IDENTITY INTEGRITY: 100%. F-2231 is a propane sit-down forklift. Location: Tennessee. The serial history is immutable.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: REMOTE-SITE VARIANCE: 0.0%. Ozzie's site: all freight reconciled. No swaps.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

entries.speaker: NARRATOR
entries.text: PRODUCTION FULFILLMENT: 100%. Kestrel Motor Works: satisfied. Line 3: operational.
entries.direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.
